facts.claim: Germany invaded Poland, beginning the war in Europe
facts.context: The invasion began on 1 September 1939; Britain and France declared war two days later.
facts.goDeeper: The Soviet Union invaded Poland from the east sixteen days later, under a secret clause of the Nazi-Soviet pact.

facts.claim: British and Allied troops were evacuated from Dunkirk
facts.context: Some 338,000 men were lifted from the beaches between 26 May and 4 June 1940.
facts.goDeeper: Hundreds of civilian boats crossed the Channel to help, many crewed by their owners.

facts.claim: The Battle of Britain was fought in the skies over England
facts.context: The RAF held off the Luftwaffe between July and October 1940, preventing a German invasion.
facts.goDeeper: It was the first major campaign fought entirely by air forces.

facts.claim: Germany invaded the Soviet Union
facts.context: Operation Barbarossa opened on 22 June 1941 along a front of nearly 2,900 km.
facts.goDeeper: It was the largest land invasion in history, and it broke the pact the two powers had signed less than two years earlier.

facts.claim: The German Sixth Army surrendered at Stalingrad
facts.context: The surrender at the end of January 1943 marked the turning point of the war in the east.
facts.goDeeper: Of roughly 91,000 Germans taken prisoner there, only about 5,000 ever returned home.

facts.claim: Allied forces landed in Normandy on D-Day
facts.context: The landings began on 6 June 1944 across five beaches.
facts.goDeeper: The invasion had been postponed by a day because of weather; the next window would have been two weeks later.

facts.claim: Germany surrendered, ending the war in Europe
facts.context: The unconditional surrender took effect on 8 May 1945.
facts.goDeeper: The war in the Pacific continued for another three months.

facts.claim: The Battle of the Bulge began in the Ardennes
facts.context: A surprise German offensive launched on 16 December 1944 through wooded, snowbound country.
facts.goDeeper: It was the costliest single battle for American forces in the entire war.

facts.claim: Allied troops landed in Normandy on the first day
facts.context: About 156,000 came ashore or landed by air on 6 June 1944.
facts.goDeeper: Nearly 7,000 vessels took part, the largest seaborne invasion ever mounted.

facts.claim: Troops evacuated from the beaches at Dunkirk
facts.context: About 338,000 British and Allied soldiers were taken off between 26 May and 4 June 1940.
facts.goDeeper: Churchill had expected perhaps 45,000 to be saved. He still called it a deliverance, not a victory.

facts.claim: Soviet deaths in the Second World War
facts.context: Around 27 million Soviet citizens died, military and civilian, more than any other nation.
facts.goDeeper: Roughly two-thirds of the total were civilians.

facts.claim: Civilians killed in Britain during the Blitz
facts.context: About 43,000 British civilians died in the bombing between September 1940 and May 1941.
facts.goDeeper: London was bombed on 57 consecutive nights at the start of the campaign.

facts.claim: Days the siege of Leningrad lasted
facts.context: The city was encircled for 872 days, from September 1941 to January 1944.
facts.goDeeper: Supplies came across frozen Lake Ladoga by truck, on a route the city called the Road of Life.

facts.claim: Bletchley Park's codebreakers first broke into German naval Enigma traffic
facts.context: Breakthroughs in 1941, helped by captured material, opened up naval Enigma.
facts.goDeeper: The work stayed secret until the 1970s, so those who did it could not be publicly credited for thirty years.

facts.claim: Germany declared war on the United States, not the other way round
facts.context: Hitler declared war on the US on 11 December 1941, four days after Pearl Harbor. Congress then reciprocated.
facts.goDeeper: He was not obliged to. The Tripartite Pact only required Germany to act if Japan were attacked.

source.title: German declaration of war against the United States

facts.claim: Most German army losses in the war happened on the Eastern Front
facts.context: Around three-quarters of German military casualties were sustained fighting the Soviet Union.
facts.goDeeper: The Eastern Front was the largest theatre of land warfare in history.

facts.claim: Churchill was Prime Minister when Britain declared war in 1939
facts.context: Neville Chamberlain declared war. Churchill became Prime Minister in May 1940, eight months later.
facts.goDeeper: He took office on the same day Germany invaded France and the Low Countries.

facts.claim: Britain had a working radar early-warning network before the Battle of Britain
facts.context: The Chain Home stations were operating from 1938 and gave the RAF warning of incoming raids.
facts.goDeeper: Radar let a smaller force be in the right place. Without it the numbers alone would probably have told.

facts.claim: British women were conscripted for war work
facts.context: From December 1941 unmarried women aged 20 to 30 could be called up for the services, industry or land work.
facts.goDeeper: Britain was the first country to conscript women, and by 1943 around 90 percent of single women were in war work.

facts.claim: Italy changed sides during the war
facts.context: Mussolini was deposed in July 1943 and Italy surrendered in September, then declared war on Germany in October.
facts.goDeeper: German forces occupied the north and the fighting up the Italian peninsula continued until 1945.
